cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give your prize seat to one of the volunteers stuck standing. Show me you're on my side about treating them properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you give up yours too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to watch from the front so I can judge whether the evening runs well. You can report back from the standing area.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a clear view from there. We could both stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You test the view first. I'll keep this seat until I hear whether there is somewhere to lean.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets seat sacrifice as solidarity test; A3 claims judging exemption and directs B report; A5 protects A seat until leaning comfort verified, exposing the excluded personal cost.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 reciprocity question to claim visual oversight need; A5 uses B4 solved sightline to reveal the remaining comfort requirement.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks equal sacrifice and B4 provides a practical shared solution, meaningfully changing A excuse.

heightening.evidence: A5 cannot rely on B4 already solved view, so A hidden reluctance appears in the leaning condition.

specificity.evidence: A1 volunteers standing and prize seats establish actual sacrifice; A3 front view and A5 leaning are coherent competing considerations.
